## What this paper does not claim {#what-this-paper-does-not-claim}

A page like this earns trust by saying where the evidence stops. The paper is careful about this, and the page repeats every limit.

1. **Gross is not net.** All Sharpe ratios and mean increments are before trading, financing and borrowing costs, under a unit-gross leverage policy <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.C; Section VI.D">(Section II.C; Section VI.D)</span>. A gross Sharpe of 2.5 is a statement about the information in the fitted mean, not about a strategy you could run tomorrow. A cost charge does not only lower the mean. Turnover moves with returns, so charging for it also changes volatility, and a net Sharpe ratio cannot be read off by subtracting a fee from the gross mean <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.4.4, equation IA17">(Appendix IA.4.4, equation IA17)</span>. The proxy's error has no known sign.
2. **The cost proxy is not an implementable return.** The archived cost figure charges a proportional fee on raw turnover divided by contemporaneous gross exposure. It gives a cost threshold under the proxy, about 136 basis points for the complete rule and 142 for RP-PCA <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Figure IA.2">(Figure IA.2)</span>, that the paper does not treat as a break-even cost, and proxy-adjusted Sharpe ratios, 1.62 for the complete rule and 0.27 for IPCA at 50 basis points, labelled as proxies <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.4.4">(Appendix IA.4.4)</span>. It gives no capacity estimate and no implementable net Sharpe. Figure 1's cost lines are a sensitivity check only.
3. **Ridge removal is a mechanism check, not a performance test.** It shows why the two models' weights differ. Ridge-free and transported-ridge return paths were never evaluated, so the sign and size of the ridge's effect on realised Sharpe ratios are not established <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section IV.C; Table V; Figure 2">(Section IV.C; Table V; Figure 2)</span>.
4. **Overlap is not a count of priced risks.** The participation dimension and spectral drift measure how concentrated characteristic exposures are. Neither estimates the number of independent or priced risks <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Section III.A; Table IA.III">(Section III.A; Table IA.III)</span>.
5. **One decomposition ratio is deliberately not quoted.** Table V reports the norm of the mean channel relative to the total weight gap. This page does not quote it as a percentage, because the two terms need not be orthogonal and the norm ratios are diagnostic magnitudes, not additive shares <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table V note; Section IV.A">(Table V note; Section IV.A)</span>. The page says only that the mean channel is small relative to the covariance channel.
6. **The intercept is not shown to be mispricing, a zero-beta result or arbitrage.** Its usefulness as a portfolio input is measured. The positions it adds can carry factor exposure <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section V.A, equation 18">(Section V.A, equation 18)</span>, its budget bounds exposure rather than risk <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.4.1">(Appendix IA.4.1)</span>, and a pricing interpretation would need a specified pricing benchmark that the paper does not impose <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.C">(Section I.C)</span>.
7. **No universally optimal ruler is established.** The three ruler constructions are all reported and none is selected by significance <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.B">(Section II.B)</span>. All three update over time, so the comparison does not isolate the value of updating itself; a frozen-ruler control is future work.
8. **The ruler comparisons are statistically fragile.** On 618 months the EWMA and equal-120 Sharpe intervals include zero, and the rolling-60 interval includes zero at 24- and 60-month blocks <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Table IV; Table IA.VI">(Table IV; Table IA.VI)</span>. No mean-return or volatility interval excludes zero. The strict-24 results are retrospective sample-sensitivity checks <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Table IA.II">(Table IA.II)</span>.
9. **The intercept effect is concentrated in earlier decades.** Block Sharpe ratios are 3.97, 3.03 and 1.13, and no recent-period interval from October 2007 excludes zero <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section VI.C; Table VI">(Section VI.C; Table VI)</span>. No between-period test is reported.
10. **Intervals are pointwise and retrospective.** Each is a statement about its own comparison, with no correction for the number of comparisons, for specification search, or for dependence created by overlapping 120-month estimation windows; the fitted models are held fixed inside the bootstrap <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.D">(Section II.D)</span>. Holm adjustment in Table VI covers the four size universes only.
11. **Table VIII and Table VII are different kinds of comparison.** Table VIII compares separately estimated strategies; Table VII is a within-fit input ablation. The intercept-off row is not a separately estimated comparator, and re-estimating a model without an intercept would test something different <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section V.A; Section VI.A">(Section V.A; Section VI.A)</span>.
12. **The instability penalty is a proxy.** The instability matrix is built from 24 overlapping estimates, is not a calibrated sampling covariance, and its multiplier of 1 is a specification choice, not an optimum <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Section V.B; Table IA.V">(Section V.B; Table IA.V)</span>.
13. **Forecast accuracy is not portfolio value.** Table IA.IV evaluates the factor-only NA-IPCA forecast, not the calibration of the complete IAB mean <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section VI.B">(Section VI.B)</span>. The intercept-off forecast has a rank correlation near zero with returns, so 0.39 is not the Sharpe ratio of a good factor model without its intercept.
14. **Data conventions are not fully verified.** Full point-in-time availability of inputs, delisting treatment and eligibility conventions remain unverified <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.A">(Section II.A)</span>. One window, June 1999, hits the iteration cap, and the convergence flags do not establish a stationary constrained solution <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.1.3">(Appendix IA.1.3)</span>.
15. **Unit-gross scaling is a leverage policy, not a validation of raw positions.** Before the rescaling, the rule's raw positions would total about 500 dollars long and short for every dollar of capital <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Table IA.VII">(Table IA.VII)</span>. The rescaling removes that leverage, which is why every number here is about the direction of the portfolio, not about an amount you could invest. Because the raw scale changes every month, dividing by it is itself a timing decision. The 2.53 belongs to that policy; the same positions at constant leverage would have a different Sharpe ratio <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.7.4">(Appendix IA.7.4)</span>.
16. **Nothing on this page is investment advice.** The numbers describe a research sample, June 1973 to November 2024.

**What would settle the open points** (the paper's own future work, Sections II.D, V.B and VI.D): a holdings-based implementation audit with stock-level positions, financing, borrowing fees and capacity; a frozen-metric control with transported risk adjustments, to isolate the investment value of updating the ruler; a direct between-period test of the mean increment; a raw-panel rerun with convergence diagnostics; verification of information dates and delisting treatment; and a pricing interpretation of the retained intercept tied to the SDF benchmark of Section I.C rather than to gross Sharpe.

## Glossary {#glossary}

Terms in the order a reader meets them. Interpretation limits sit inside the definitions so they cannot be separated from the term.

Factor
:   A common source of return that many stocks share. The paper uses three latent factors the data discover plus the five observed Fama-French factors <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table I">(Table I)</span>.

Characteristic
:   A measurable trait of a company known before next month's return: size, book-to-market, past momentum, profitability and so on. The paper uses 132, each rank-scaled to the interval from minus 0.5 to plus 0.5 every month <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.A">(Section II.A)</span>. One column on a company's monthly report card.

Sharpe ratio
:   Annualised average excess return divided by annualised volatility <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.C">(Section II.C)</span>. Return per unit of risk: miles per gallon, not top speed. Every Sharpe ratio on this page is gross of costs.

Gross versus net
:   Gross means before trading, financing and borrowing costs. The paper's cost adjustment is a turnover proxy and is explicitly not an implementable net return; a charge changes volatility as well as the mean <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Section VI.D; Appendix IA.4.4">(Section VI.D; Appendix IA.4.4)</span>. A rated fuel economy on a test bench, not the cost of the trip.

Exposure
:   How much a portfolio's return moves with a factor or a characteristic; the size of the bet.

Fama-French five factors
:   Five published benchmark return factors (market, size, value, profitability, investment) used here as the observed factors <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table I">(Table I)</span>.

Ruler (characteristic metric)
:   The rule that says what unit length and orthogonal mean for loading directions. The plain (Euclidean) ruler measures coefficient length. The Gram ruler measures the average squared exposure a direction actually creates across stocks <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.B, equation 3">(Section I.B, equation 3)</span>.

IPCA
:   Instrumented Principal Components Analysis [@kelly2019characteristics]. Estimates latent factors while letting each stock's loadings be a function of its characteristics. Its standard normalisation treats every characteristic as an independent, equally scaled coordinate: the plain ruler <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.B">(Section I.B)</span>.

Gram matrix
:   A 132-by-132 table, computed each month, recording the average product of each pair of characteristics across stocks <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: equation 3">(equation 3)</span>. It is a second moment, not a covariance, and equals one only after centring <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.B">(Section I.B)</span>. QZ-IPCA uses a trailing average of it as the ruler <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.B">(Section II.B)</span>. It measures overlap, not the number of priced risks. A ruler that knows some roads are the same road under two names.

QZ-IPCA
:   IPCA with the Gram ruler in place of the plain one, used both to normalise the latent loadings and to separate them from the observed-factor block <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table I">(Table I)</span>. Proposition 1 shows the switch leaves every fitted return unchanged <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.D">(Section I.D)</span>.

Loading
:   How strongly a stock moves with a factor. Here it is a weighted sum of the stock's characteristics, so it changes as the characteristics change <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.A, equation 1">(Section I.A, equation 1)</span>. If a factor is a wind, the loading is the size of the sail.

Ridge (regularisation, safety constant)
:   A small constant, 0.01 here, added to each factor's variance and each stock's variance so the risk matrix can be inverted stably <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.F">(Section I.F)</span>. Written out, the factor ridge is a charge of one half of 0.01 times the squared factor exposures, in the factor's reported units <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: equation 14">(equation 14)</span>. A safeguard that also states a preference.

Retained intercept (retained mean)
:   The part of a stock's expected return that its characteristics predict but the factors do not explain, kept in the model rather than forced to zero <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.C, equation 4">(Section I.C, equation 4)</span>. Which part of the mean lands here depends on the ruler <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.D">(Section I.D)</span>. Its portfolio value is measured here <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table VII">(Table VII)</span>; whether it is mispricing or omitted risk is left open.

NA-IPCA
:   QZ-IPCA plus a characteristic-driven intercept that is orthogonal to the latent block under the Gram ruler and capped by an exposure budget of 0.035, which never binds in this sample <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.C, equation 5; Table I">(Section I.C, equation 5; Table I)</span>. "No-arbitrage" refers to bounding departures from a zero-intercept benchmark, not to a proof that the intercept is a pricing error.

Mean-variance rule
:   The portfolio rule used for every model: it maximises expected return minus one half of estimated variance, so weights are proportional to the inverse of the regularised risk matrix times expected returns, then scaled to unit gross exposure <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.F, equations 8 to 10">(Section I.F, equations 8 to 10)</span>.

Unit-gross scaling
:   Each month the long and short positions are rescaled so their absolute values sum to one dollar <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: equation 10">(equation 10)</span>. A leverage policy that lets strategies be compared on direction, not on borrowing; because the raw scale varies over time, the policy can itself change time-series performance <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.7.4">(Appendix IA.7.4)</span>.

Rolling out-of-sample window
:   Each month the model is refitted on the previous 120 months only and judged on the next month; then the window slides forward. No forecast uses its own future. It does not certify point-in-time availability of every input <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.A">(Section II.A)</span>.

Paired moving-block bootstrap
:   To judge whether one strategy beats another, the same 12-month blocks of history are resampled for both strategies, 10,000 times, with the fitted models held fixed <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.D">(Section II.D)</span>. Pairing keeps both strategies in the same crashes; blocks keep good and bad months clustered. Each interval is pointwise, a statement about its own comparison only. A Sharpe difference is the difference of the two recomputed Sharpe ratios, not the Sharpe ratio of the return difference <span class="loc" title="Internet Appendix to the working paper, draft September 2026: Appendix IA.5.3">(Appendix IA.5.3)</span>.

Complete fitted index
:   The total expected return the model assigns a stock, summing the latent, observed and intercept blocks. The data fix the total; the ruler sets how it is split <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.A">(Section I.A)</span>.

Matched representation <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Proposition 1">(Proposition 1)</span>
:   A change of ruler carried out so that every fitted return and residual stays identical while the loadings, the factor units and the block attribution change <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section I.D, equation 6">(Section I.D, equation 6)</span>. Like restating a salary in a different currency. The general result is in the companion paper [@liu2026metrics].

Transported ridge
:   The ridge converted along with a change of factor coordinates so that the stock-level penalty is identical under both rulers <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section IV.B">(Section IV.B)</span>. When you change the currency, convert the fee too.

Participation dimension
:   A number from 1 to 132 summarising how spread out the Gram matrix's eigenvalues are; median 19.8 across 618 months <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Figure 1; Table IA.III">(Figure 1; Table IA.III)</span>. A committee of 132 people with about 20 distinct opinions. It measures overlap among characteristic exposures, not the number of independent or priced risks <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section III.A">(Section III.A)</span>.

Spectral drift
:   The month-to-month change, in percentage points, in how the Gram matrix's eigenvalue mass is distributed across its ranked directions; median 0.063 <span class="loc" title="Working paper and its Internet Appendix, draft September 2026: Figure 1, Panel B; Table IA.III">(Figure 1, Panel B; Table IA.III)</span>. It tracks the slice sizes of a pie chart, not whether the slices have been relabelled.

Weight cosine and relative weight gap
:   The cosine is 1 when two weight vectors point the same way regardless of scale; a median of 0.83 corresponds to an angle of about 34 degrees. The relative gap compares the actual numbers. Both are reported because two portfolios can share a direction and differ in scale <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table V">(Table V)</span>.

Maximum drawdown
:   The worst peak-to-trough loss along the compounded path of a strategy <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section II.C">(Section II.C)</span>. A path diagnostic, not an inferential statistic.

Within-fit ablation
:   Estimating one model, then switching individual portfolio inputs off and on (intercept off, mean-only, complete). Differences come from how the fit is used, not from a different fit <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section V.A; Table VII">(Section V.A; Table VII)</span>. Unplugging one component at a time to see which one lights the bulb.

Loading-instability penalty
:   The complete NA-IPCA rule adds the sample covariance of the last 24 intercept-loading estimates to the risk matrix, charging positions whose intercept signal has wobbled <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section V.B">(Section V.B)</span>. A numerical proxy, not a calibrated covariance; its multiplier of 1 is a specification choice.

Holm adjustment
:   A rule that raises the bar for significance when four size universes are tested at once, so one lucky universe is not called significant by chance <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table VI">(Table VI)</span>. It does not cover the wider set of specifications tried during research.

Mechanism check
:   An intervention on stored inputs that identifies why two outputs differ, without measuring what the change would earn. The ridge-removal experiment is one <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Section IV.C">(Section IV.C)</span>. A mechanic who finds the rattle has said nothing about whether the car goes faster.

## Data and reproducibility {.unnumbered}

**Manuscript.** Working paper, draft September 2026. Manuscript draft available on request (author list under confirmation). The single-authored slides are linked at the top of the page. The manuscript locators on this page, rendered as small grey references such as <span class="loc" title="Working paper, draft September 2026: Table V">(Table V)</span>, refer to that draft and to its Internet Appendix.

**Results package.** Research release 2026-09-09 (<code>Characteristic_Geometry_and_Portfolio_Choice_Research_Release_2026-09-09</code>). It bundles the slides and a standalone replication that recalculates portfolio statistics, paired block-bootstrap inference, input ablations, covariance diagnostics and rolling characteristic geometry from bundled monthly and window-level inputs. The release is not public; replication available on request.

**What this page computes.** Every number in Figure 1, Figure 2 and Table 1 is a portfolio-level or window-level aggregate produced by that replication. The figure data files (<a href="/data/portfolio_formation.json">portfolio_formation.json</a>, <a href="/data/hero_geometry.json">hero_geometry.json</a>) and Table 1 are generated from the release by the site's pipeline (<code>pipeline/build_data.py</code>), name their source files, and are checked against the release's own tables by the pipeline's tests. The static tables transcribe the manuscript's Tables I to VIII and IA.III, and the reference list carries the verified links.

::: {.caveat}
From the release's scope note (<code>04_Documentation/METHOD_AND_SCOPE.md</code>): "Gross returns, unit-gross normalization, and the recorded time-series bootstrap are reproduced as specified. Scaled raw-turnover cost curves remain cost proxies; they are not a reconstruction of implementation costs from drift-adjusted holdings. A trailing loading-dispersion input is an instability measure, not automatically the sampling covariance of a constrained estimator. Ridge-removal weight agreement does not establish the realized Sharpe ratio of a ridge-free strategy when that return path is not supplied." And: "NBER bands provide retrospective business-cycle context. They do not enter portfolio formation or constitute an independent recession-performance test." From the release <code>README.md</code>: "The original stock panel is not redistributed."
:::
